name: Command-line tool or library
summary: A package with a clean public API and a thin command-line interface on top, tested across versions and published to its registry with automated releases. Go, Python and Rust shown; pick the one the users install.

fitsWhen.says: it runs on the user's machine

avoidWhen.says: people use it through a UI
it needs accounts or live data

backend.why: Subcommands, flags, help and shell completions; Typer for Python, clap for Rust.

ci-cd.why: Cross-compiled binaries, checksums, Homebrew formula and a changelog from tags.

testing.why: Golden-file tests of command output plus unit tests of the library.

hosting.why: Published to the language's registry; docs on a static site.

observability.why: Optional and off by default; a CLI should not phone home.

services.name: lib
responsibilities: No I/O it was not asked to do

environments.name: staging
environments.purpose: A release candidate tag installed from the registry's test index

stages.name: test
stages.does: Tests on Linux, macOS and Windows

security.auth: Credentials read from the environment or the OS keychain, never from flags (they end up in shell history)
security.secrets: Release signing keys in CI secrets
notes: Dependencies pinned and updated by Renovate

folderLayout:
cmd/tool/main.go
internal/cli/
pkg/tool/  (the public library)
testdata/
.goreleaser.yaml
conventions: Semantic versioning; the public API changes only in a major release

adrs.title: Library first, CLI second
adrs.decision: All behaviour lives in the library; the CLI only parses and prints.
adrs.why: Other programs can use the library, and tests do not need to run the binary.

repos.label: tool
repos.layout: A Go module with a Cobra CLI (adapt to Python or Rust if chosen)

files.template: Install, usage examples and the exit codes.
Root command with --json and --verbose flags and a version subcommand.
A table-driven test of that function.
Builds for linux, darwin and windows on amd64 and arm64 with checksums.
Lint and test on three operating systems; release on tags.
